name: Saifuddin Firuz Shah
seoTitle: Saifuddin Firuz Shah: Habshi Sultan of Bengal, 1487–1489
seoDescription: Saifuddin Firuz Shah, formerly the commander Malik Andil, was a Habshi ruler of Bengal associated with the transition from Ilyas Shahi rule to the short Habshi dynasty.
role: Habshi Sultan of Bengal and former military commander
contribution: Saifuddin Firuz Shah, formerly Malik Andil, rose from the Bengal Sultanate's military establishment and took the throne in 1487 after the brief rule of Shahzada Barbak. His accession began a short Habshi phase in Bengal's late-fifteenth-century politics before the Hussain Shahi dynasty in 1494.
context: The late Ilyas Shahi crisis and the brief Habshi rule centred on Gaur, when palace and military commanders played a growing role in succession politics.
impact: The surviving architectural and inscriptional record links his reign with Firuz Minar and mosque construction around Gaur and Maldah. His career shows how Habshi military elites could move from the Sultanate's command structure to the throne during a period of dynastic instability.
